title: Use AI to make what AI produces easier to understand, at every level of detail. Build things that get better as AI models get better.
subtitle: Open a topic to see its projects. Each project has a short video of about two minutes that plays on this page, with its full videos, website and code beside it.

doors.question: What has AI proved that Lean has checked?
doors.caption: A case of an Erdős problem from 1968, OpenAI's quantum query bound and a spin-glass theorem, each with a Lean proof.

doors.question: Which sentences in a paper does its Lean proof cover?
doors.caption: Click a sentence to open the Lean lines it describes, and see which statements each proof covers in full.

doors.question: What did the coding agent run, change and commit?
doors.caption: Claude Code and Codex sessions: each command beside its output, one agent's commit beside another's edits, a hook that blocks a commit.

doors.question: How does one Lean proof become papers and a video?
doors.caption: One proof becomes a 152-page research record, a 26-page paper, a 16-page exposition and a video, each picture timed to a spoken word.

doors.question: Which function calls this one, and what does each file do?
doors.caption: A map of the descriptions agents write in each file, and a database of calls that NVIDIA Auto Ontology queries in SQL.

doors.question: Do a model's tests catch more bugs when its prompt lists the bugs it missed?
doors.caption: On 58 new problems, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash caught 77% of bugs instead of 69%.
